papers.title_en: Introduction to Stochastic Differential Equations for Generative Machine Learning: A Variational Perspective
papers.authors: Ole Winther, Paul Jeha, Sander Dieleman, Andriy Mnih, Manfred Opper, Andrea Dittadi
papers.evidence: 生成式SDE导论，涵盖扩散和流匹配，为流体动力学奠定基础
papers.tldr: 生成机器学习需模拟复杂数据分布，传统方法存在局限性。本文从变分视角出发，利用随机微分方程（SDE）和Fokker-Planck方程，推导出证据下界（ELBO），将扩散模型、得分匹配和流匹配统一为变分特例。通过一维密度建模示例比较不同参数化，展示了统一框架的灵活性和有效性。该自包含介绍为理解生成模型的微分方程基础提供了清晰路径。
papers.abstract_en: The use of ordinary and stochastic differential equations has led to substantial progress in generative machine learning with applications to, for example, image, video and biomolecule generation. This paper provides a self-contained and informal introduction to the differential equations, the probabilistic framework for using them in generative modeling and the Fokker--Planck equation that governs the temporal evolution of the marginal distribution of the stochastic variables of the differential equations. The variational lower bound on the log-likelihood (the evidence lower bound, ELBO) is derived and used as a general starting point for a discussion of diffusion models, score matching, and flow matching. All of these approaches may be viewed as specific parameterizations of the most general variational approach. A one-dimensional density modeling problem is used as a simple example to compare different parameterizations.
